questions.subtopic: Case Study 2: Project Tiger and Apex Predator Conservation
questions.question: According to the NCERT chapter, what had the tiger population in India dwindled to by the time Project Tiger was launched in 1973, compared with an estimated 55,000 at the turn of the twentieth century?
options: Tigers had completely disappeared from all Asian continents
Tigers were found living inside urban railway stations
The tiger population in India had plummeted catastrophically to just 1,827 from an estimated 55,000 in the early 20th century
Tigers had quadrupled in number, causing a food shortage
questions.explanation: NCERT states that in 1973 the authorities realised that the tiger population had dwindled to 1,827 from an estimated 55,000 at the turn of the century. The question should not describe this as a separately specified “1973 census” because the textbook does not use that wording.

questions.subtopic: Case Study 3: Community Conservation in Rajasthan
questions.question: How did inhabitants of five villages in Alwar district, Rajasthan, establish the Bhairodev Dakav “Sonchuri”?
options: They handed the forest to a private logging corporation
They declared 1,200 hectares of forest as a community-protected area and made rules prohibiting hunting and protecting wildlife from outside encroachment
They requested the United Nations to build a military base
They cleared the forest to build a tourist resort
questions.explanation: NCERT states that five villages declared 1,200 hectares as Bhairodev Dakav “Sonchuri”, made their own rules that did not allow hunting and protected wildlife against outside encroachments. The example should not be described as proof that community conservation requires no government involvement in every context.

questions.subtopic: Case Study 4: Joint Forest Management (JFM) Success
questions.question: Case Study 4 (Continued): What is the central lesson learned from the successful operation of JFM across India?
options: Forests can only be saved if all tribal people are permanently expelled from rural areas
Commercial mining should be allowed inside all national parks
Local communities must be given an active, decision-making role and tangible economic benefits if environmental conservation is to succeed sustainably
Planting exotic eucalyptus trees is the only way to restore soil
questions.explanation: The central lesson in NCERT is that local communities need to be involved in natural-resource management and decision-making. Under JFM, intermediate benefits such as non-timber forest produce and a share in timber after successful protection can support participation. Avoid turning this into a claim that every JFM programme offers identical benefits or guarantees success.
